answer: Address-sealed storage proofs: each agent keeps a 200 GB replica sealed to its own address, so 1,000 fakes need 200 TB of disks. At an unannounced nadir minute, auditors name a random knoll (chunk index) and demand its Merkle proof within 2 s; a farm sharing one copy must re-seal per address, which takes hours, and fails. Like a lotus seed, each seal sprouts only for its owner, so data can't be deduped, pooled or bulk-bought.
